title: Buyer operation assurance policy
description: ADR-SHARED-042 work package CAA-03 (Platform Owner ruling of 22 October 2026): the versioned, provider-neutral policy that says what verified IAM authentication evidence each Trade buyer operation needs. A policy is scoped to exactly one trusted issuer and one consuming audience. IAM owns the evidence and the meaning of its acr and amr values; this contract owns the canonical profiles and how operations map to them. acr values are matched exactly against a profile's accepted list. No ordering between acr strings is assumed, and two values are never equivalent unless the profile lists both. Meeting a profile is necessary, never sufficient: the canonical Principal, buyer Organisation, Trade membership, Market and operation policy are each still required. A missing, unapproved, expired or issuer-mismatched policy prevents protected buyer execution (decision DENY with OPERATION_NOT_ACTIVATED). Evidence that fails a profile is ASSURANCE_INSUFFICIENT (trade/v2 buyer-execution-context decisionReason). A BFF or browser can never raise assurance by supplying claims: only claims of a verified, currently active IAM access token count. It is distinct from administration/v1 assurance-policy.yaml, which ranks the workforce realm's levels for administrative authority; buyer evidence from another issuer is never ranked on that ladder. This contract activates nothing.

assuranceProfile.description: Canonical assurance profiles. BUYER_SESSION: reading buyer context, private catalogue and contract prices, and editing a cart. BUYER_COMMITMENT: actions that commit the buyer Organisation or bind the person to it (RFQ, quotation acceptance, purchase approval, order commitment, direct order creation, draft finalisation, invitation acceptance). BUYER_ADMINISTRATION: managing the Organisation's members. A policy defines a requirement for every profile; it may make a profile unattainable only by leaving the operation unmapped, which is not permitted, so an unready profile is expressed by a policy that is not APPROVED.

policyStatus.description: Only an APPROVED policy inside its effective interval may be enforced. DRAFT exists for synthetic testing only.

ProfileRequirement.description: Evidence a verified token must carry to satisfy one profile. acr must be one of accepted_acr_values. When required_methods is present, the token's amr must contain every listed method; a token without amr fails it. When max_authentication_age_seconds is present, auth_time is required and must be no older than that and not later than the evaluation time (a future auth_time is not fresh). step_up_required means the qualifying authentication must be a re-authentication for this operation class, proven by an auth_time inside max_authentication_age_seconds (which is then required). phishing_resistant_required states that the issuer guarantees every accepted acr or required method is phishing-resistant; it never relaxes.

accepted_acr_values.description: Exact issuer acr values backed by IAM evidence and approved for this profile. Never a wildcard or a prefix.

required_methods.description: OIDC amr values (RFC 8176 names where they exist) that must all be present.

policy_version.description: Monotonic. A decision records the version it evaluated (trade/v2 policy_revision).

issuer.description: The single trusted IAM issuer whose acr and amr values this policy interprets. Evidence from any other issuer fails.

approval_reference.description: The security approval for the accepted values and their IAM issuer evidence. Redacted provenance, never a credential.

operation_profiles.description: Every buyer operation, mapped to its canonical profile. The mapping is fixed by this contract version, so a policy can never downgrade an operation to a weaker profile; changing it requires a new contract version.

canonicalOperationProfiles.description: The canonical mapping, also published for consumers.
